chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Prayer is not performed in the valley of Al-Shuqrah.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.وَادِي الشُّقْرَةِ: The valley of Al-Shuqrah, a specific location mentioned in hadith literature.
key_terms.يُصَلَّى: Prayer is performed (passive verb from salat).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in the valley of Al-Shuqrah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the prohibition of praying in Wadi al-Shuqrah, a valley near Mecca known for its distinct topography and historical association with pre-Islamic practices. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that certain physical environments may carry specific ritual impurities or distractions, thereby influencing the validity or preference of the prayer location.
